usage: Usually used as a countable noun when you mean a pearl as a gemstone or a bead from an oyster. In daily Cantonese, it often appears in compound words and jewellery-related phrases.
Common with words like 珍珠項鏈, 珍珠耳環, and 珍珠粉. It sounds neutral and natural in both speaking and writing.
When talking about quality, people may describe size, shape, shine, and colour of 珍珠. It is a very common word in fashion, accessories, and beauty contexts.
Learners should remember that 珍珠 is the standard word for "pearl"; it is not used for fake pearl in a special grammatical way, so context decides whether it is real or imitation.
